outline.chapter_title: Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models
outline.description: Introduces why reinforcement learning has become important for scaling language models, the kinds of reasoning tasks it improves, and the central stability problem that motivates GSPO.
subtopics: Why post-training with RL matters for modern language models
Examples of RL-driven gains in math, coding, and long-form reasoning
The scaling perspective: more compute, longer rollouts, larger models
Training stability as the main bottleneck in large-scale RL
Catastrophic model collapse in existing RL algorithms
How this paper positions GSPO as a response to GRPO instability
Overview of the paper's claims: stability, efficiency, performance, and infrastructure simplification

outline.chapter_title: Core Foundations: Policies, Rewards, and Off-Policy Optimization
outline.description: Builds the mathematical background needed to understand the paper, including autoregressive policies, sequence likelihoods, reward modeling, and the role of importance sampling in off-policy RL.
subtopics: Autoregressive language models as policies
Queries, responses, datasets, and verifier-based rewards
Token likelihood versus sequence likelihood
What it means to optimize a response-level reward
On-policy and off-policy learning in language-model RL
Why rollout batches are split into mini-batches during training
The basic principle of importance sampling
When importance reweighting is valid and why sample averaging matters
Clipping as a safeguard against overly off-policy updates

outline.chapter_title: PPO and GRPO: The Starting Point
outline.description: Explains the two baseline algorithms behind the paper: PPO as the standard clipped policy-gradient method, and GRPO as a value-model-free variant designed for LLM RL.
subtopics: Review of the PPO objective
Token-level importance ratios in PPO
Advantage estimation with a learned value model
Why value models are costly and difficult to scale for LLMs
The motivation for Group Relative Policy Optimization
GRPO's group-based sampling over multiple responses per query
Normalized group rewards as response-level advantages
The GRPO objective and its token-level clipping
Strengths of GRPO: avoiding a value model
The paper's setup for comparing GSPO against GRPO

outline.description: Diagnoses the paper's central criticism of GRPO: its token-level importance ratios are ill-posed for response-level rewards and inject high-variance noise that grows with sequence length.
subtopics: The mismatch between reward granularity and optimization granularity
Why GRPO uses a single response-level advantage for every token
The paper's claim that token-level importance ratios are misapplied
Importance sampling over distributions versus single sampled tokens
How token-level noise accumulates over long responses
How clipping can amplify rather than fix the instability
Why instability becomes worse with larger models and longer generations
Empirical symptoms: collapse, irreversibility, and failed recovery attempts
The design principle: the optimization unit should match the reward unit

outline.chapter_title: The GSPO Algorithm: Sequence-Level Policy Optimization
outline.description: Presents GSPO in full, showing how it replaces token-level correction with sequence-level likelihood ratios and aligns clipping, rewarding, and optimization at the response level.
subtopics: The core idea of sequence-level importance ratios
The GSPO objective and its sequence-level clipping rule
Group-normalized rewards as advantages
Defining the sequence ratio from policy likelihoods
Why the ratio is length-normalized
Geometric-mean interpretation of the normalized sequence ratio
Numerical stability and unified clipping across different response lengths
How GSPO excludes overly off-policy responses rather than individual tokens
Why GSPO's clipping ranges differ in magnitude from GRPO's
Conceptual alignment between sequence reward and sequence optimization

outline.chapter_title: Gradient-Level Comparison Between GSPO and GRPO
outline.description: Derives and interprets the gradients of GSPO and GRPO to make clear why the algorithms behave differently in practice.
subtopics: Deriving the GSPO gradient without clipping
How the sequence ratio scales all tokens in a response equally
Deriving the GRPO gradient without clipping
How GRPO assigns different weights to different tokens
The role of token-wise likelihood ratios in gradient noise
Why unequal token weighting can accumulate harmful effects
Positive and negative advantage regions under clipping
Interpreting GSPO as a more coherent response-level credit assignment mechanism
What the gradient analysis suggests about training stability

outline.description: Introduces GSPO-token, a variant designed for settings that need token-wise advantages while preserving the sequence-level importance ratio that stabilizes learning.
subtopics: Why multi-turn or structured tasks may need token-level advantage control
The GSPO-token objective
The stop-gradient or detach trick in the ratio definition
Why the token factor is numerically equal to one
Gradient derivation for GSPO-token
How GSPO-token preserves sequence-level weighting while allowing token-wise advantages
Equivalence between GSPO and GSPO-token when all token advantages are equal
When to prefer GSPO versus GSPO-token in practice

outline.description: Explains how the paper evaluates GSPO, including the model, training procedure, benchmarks, metrics, and hyperparameter choices needed for a fair comparison.
subtopics: The cold-start model based on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base
Rollout generation and four-way mini-batch partitioning
Why the training regime is naturally off-policy
Benchmarks: AIME'24, LiveCodeBench, and CodeForces
Evaluation metrics: Pass@1 and Elo rating
Clipping ranges used for GSPO and GRPO
Fairness considerations in hyperparameter tuning
The role of query refresh and generation-length extension during training

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Results: Stability, Efficiency, and Performance
outline.description: Covers the main empirical findings of the paper, showing that GSPO trains more stably, uses training compute more effectively, and scales better than GRPO.
subtopics: Reward-curve behavior under GSPO versus GRPO
Evidence of stable training throughout long RL runs
Continuous gains from increasing training compute

outline.chapter_title: Clipping Behavior and What It Reveals
outline.description: Examines the paper's surprising observation that GSPO clips far more tokens than GRPO yet still learns better, and uses this to interpret the quality of the learning signal in both methods.
subtopics: Sequence-level clipping versus token-level clipping
Observed differences in clipping fractions across the two algorithms

outline.chapter_title: Mixture-of-Experts Training and the End of Routing Replay
outline.description: Explains why MoE models are especially difficult for token-level policy optimization, how Routing Replay was previously used to stabilize GRPO, and why GSPO removes the need for that workaround.

outline.chapter_title: Practical Implications for RL Systems and Infrastructure
